out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: PIC Duties, Train Employees on Holding Temps
violations.observation: Employees are not routinely monitoring the temperatures of Time/Temperature Control for Safety foods during cold holding for multiple TCS food items stored on prep counter throughout the prepline.
violations.corrective_action: The Person in Charge or Certified Food Manager shall designate employees to monitor the cold holding and hot holding of time/temperature control for safety foods. The employees shall be trained in using a calibrated food thermometer to ensure proper temperatures. EHS will schedule follow up to check if a system has been put into place to ensure all TCS food items are cold holding at 41F or below throughout service.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS provided printed copy of the written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility sink basin is storing a wiping cloth bucket located near the 3 vat sink is blocked, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. CDI: CFM relocated wiping cloth bucket from hand sink basin to allow easy access for food prep employees to wash their hands.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at the handwashing sink near the 3 vat sink..
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. CDI: CFM provided paper towels at the hand sink.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: uncooked sliced beef stored above cooked rice inside the Dukers 2 Dr preptop refrigerator on the prep line,
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: CFM relocated the cooked rice to a shelf above the uncooked beef inside the Dukers 2 Dr preptop refrigerator. PHO HAI DUONG RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 07/23/2026) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: beef soup (120F) hot holding in metal pot on top of stovetop on cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI: CFM slightly turned up burner on stovetop to reheat beef soup to 212F for hot holding.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: pork and shrimp summer spring rolls (79F) in plastic container, container of unsalted butter (78F), diced garlic & oil (77F) in metal containers on prep counter at room temperature. EHS observed cooked sliced pork (44F) and overfilled bag of cut lettuce (47F) inside top part of the Dukers 2 Dr preptop on the prepline. EHS observed overfilled bag of lettuce not properly stored in the top part of the preptop refrigerator containers.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated container of spring rolls, unsalted butter and diced garlic and oil to the walk-in refrigerator cool to 41F or below. CFM stated they will purchase salted butter going forward. CFM relocated cooked sliced pork to walk in refrigerator to properly cool to 41F or below and removed some the lettuce of bag and placed bag of lettuce inside the container of the preptop refrigerator.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restriction & Storage; Medicines Location
violations.observation: Employees' medicines are not properly located to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. Observed multiple medications stored in a container designated as “employee” stored in such a way that they could contaminate dry food items on the dry storage shelf in the front main kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Employees' medicines shall be properly stored to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. CDI: CFM relocated container containing mediations and employee items to area away from dry storage.

violations.title: Restricted Use Pesticide, Conditions of use
violations.observation: Restricted, commercial use pesticides (insect repellant spray bottle) present in the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Because of their toxicity, restricted use pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using and remove insect repellant spray bottle from the facility.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: bulk dry items (sugar, flour, salt, corn starch) not easily identifiable stored in plastic bins throughout the main kitchen and metal containers on the cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CDI: CFM added common food labels to dry bulk food items in bulk plastic bins and metal containers on the cookline.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Plastic bulk bins of food stored on the floor inside the walk in freezer. Soybean oil x 2 stored on the floor in the front main kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS instructed CFM to relocated plastic bulk bins of food to shelves inside the walk in freezer and relocate soybean oil x 2 to shelf on prep counter in the main kitchen area.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: EHS observed food employee wearing jewelry on their arms and hands (watch) while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. CDI: EHS instructed to use hair restraints when preparing food.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: In-use knives improperly stored equipment (prep counters and refrigerated cold hold units on the prep line in between use.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CDI: CFM washed, rinsed, and sanitized knives before relocating them to clean contact surface in between use.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items Storage and Handling
violations.observation: Unwrapped knives, forks, or spoons were found handled, displayed or dispensed with the food or lip-contact surface facing different directions in plastic bin near the main kitchen entrance and front service area.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items and cleaned/sanitized utensils shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food and lip contact surfaces are prevented. EHS instructed CFM to arrange all unwrapped utensils in the same direction to prevent exposing to lip-contact part.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: trash bags covering prep counter where egg rolls are prepared; plastic bins throughout with holes in storing food items inside the walk in refrigerator, sticker on oven, non-food grade plastic drawer storing fresh herbs in front prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS scheduled follow up. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using plastic drawer to store fresh herbs. EHS scheduled follow up. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using nonfood grade plastic bin to store fresh herbs.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storing food items in the walk in freezer and various items in the back dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EHS instructed CFM to discontinue using and remove milk crates for storage going forward.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: An air gap between the water supply outlet at the 1 sink basin prep sink and the flood rim level is not observed in the front kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. EHS instructed CFM to cut white piping under prep sink to create appropriate spacing for air gap between piping system and flood rim of drain underneath. EHS has scheduled follow up inspection

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Maintenance Tools Storage
violations.observation: Maintenance tools (broom, dust pan) are leaning against dry storage food items stored on dry storage shelf in a way that prevents the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service items in the front kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Store all maintenance tools in a manner that prevents contamination of food and food-contact surfaces. CDI: CFM relocated broom and dust pan to area away from dry food storage area.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. CDI: EHS texted CFM copy of employee health policy to review information with staff, sign, and maintain on file for future reference.
